newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone, Coca-Cola announce fruit juice venture.
newsitem.headline: Danone, Coca-Cola announce fruit juice venture.

text.p: French food giant Danone and Coca-Cola Foods announced an agreement Tuesday to create a chilled fruit juice venture capitalising on their trademark Minute Maid and Danone brands.
The venture, named Minute Maid Danone, will be based in France and focus initially on European and Latin American markets, the companies said in a joint statement.
The venture brings together the brand strength of the two industry heavyweights.

Coca-Cola Foods, a division of Atlanta-based Coca-Cola Co., is the world leader in fruit juices and drinks. Danone, best known for its yogurts and dairy products, is the biggest French food company and ranks seventh worldwide.
The companies said the chilled juice products, labelled Minute Maid -- a Coca-Cola trademark -- and Danone, would not be sold in the United States and Canada.
Terms of the venture were not disclosed but it was scheduled to launch drinks products, supplied by Coca-Cola's Brazilian partner Sucocitrico Cutrale Ltda, in the first half of 1997.

"Consumers throughout North America look to the Minute Maid brand for the best in taste, value and nutrition, and consumers around the world look to the Danone brand as a guarantee of health, freshness and quality," Ralph Cooper, president of Coca-Cola Foods, said in the statement.
He said the venture was part of Coca-Cola Foods' strategy to market refrigerated juices in 50 countries by the year 2000.
Danone chairman Franck Riboud said the agreement fit with its international development plans. "We want Danone to be one of the world's brand standards," he said.

The French group has been active in the past year forming dairy, biscuit and other ventures in the Middle East and Latin America to reduce its dependence on the slow-growing European market, which accounts for three-quarters of its turnover.
Danone shares were up 10 francs at 727 on the Paris bourse in early trading. Coca-Cola shares were up 25 cents at $51.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
